pois.name: Gediminas Tower
pois.reason: Brick castle tower on the hill above the Old Town; views from the top
pois.hook: Last remnant of the Upper Castle, once pictured on the Lithuanian litas.
pois.description: Gediminas's Tower is the remaining part of the Upper Castle on top of the Gediminas Hill in Vilnius, Lithuania. It has a viewing platform that offers scenic views of Vilnius Old Town and Vilnius Central Business District.

pois.name: St Anne's Church
pois.reason: Gothic church in ornate red brick
pois.hook: Flamboyant Gothic in red brick, built around 1495–1500 by the Vilnia.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Anne in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: St. Anne's Church Exterior 3, Vilnius, Lithuania - Diliff.jpg
pois.description: St. Anne's Church is a Roman Catholic church in Vilnius' Old Town, on the right bank of the Vilnia river established circa 1495–1500. It is a prominent example of both Flamboyant and Brick Gothic styles.

pois.name: Gate of Dawn
pois.reason: Last surviving city gate; chapel with a revered icon above the arch
pois.hook: The city's last surviving gate, with a revered icon in a chapel above the arch.
pois.description: The Gate of Dawn is a city gate in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania, and one of its most important religious, historical and cultural monuments. It is a major site of Catholic pilgrimage in Lithuania.

pois.name: National Museum of Lithuania
pois.reason: Lithuanian history in the New Arsenal at the foot of Castle Hill
pois.hook: Lithuanian history in the New Arsenal, from a collection of 1.5 million items.
pois.description: The National Museum of Lithuania, established in 1952, is a state-sponsored historical museum that encompasses several significant structures and a wide collection of written materials and artifacts. It also organizes archeological digs in Lithuania.

pois.name: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania
pois.reason: Rebuilt palace of the grand dukes behind the Cathedral
pois.hook: Grand dukes' palace for four centuries, demolished in 1801 and since rebuilt.
pois.commonsCategory: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania
pois.description: The Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania is a palace in Vilnius, Lithuania. It was originally constructed in the 15th century for the rulers of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the future Kings of Poland.

pois.name: Vilnius Cathedral
pois.hook: Seat of the bishops of Vilnius since the 14th century.
pois.localName: Vilniaus Šv. Stanislovo ir Šv. Vladislovo arkikatedra bazilika
pois.description: The Vilnius Cathedral, formally the Archcathedral Basilica of St. Stanislaus and St. Ladislaus, is the Roman Catholic cathedral of the Archdiocese of Vilnius and a minor basilica in Vilnius, Lithuania.

pois.name: House of the Signatories
pois.reason: Where Lithuania's 1918 independence act was signed
pois.hook: Lithuania's Act of Independence was signed here on 16 February 1918.
pois.description: The House of the Signatories is a Lithuanian historic landmark on Pilies Street, Vilnius, where on February 16, 1918, the Act of Independence of Lithuania was signed by twenty members of the Council of Lithuania.

pois.name: Hill of Three Crosses
pois.reason: White crosses on a hill with one of the best views of the Old Town
pois.hook: Crosses for martyred friars, dynamited by the Soviets in 1950, rebuilt in 1989.
pois.commonsImage: The Hill of Three Crosses, Vilnius (55176284797).jpg
pois.description: Three Crosses is a prominent monument in Vilnius, Lithuania, on the Hill of Three Crosses, also known as the Bald Hill or Crooked Hill, in Kalnai Park. According to a legend, which finds its source in some historic events, seven Franciscan friars were beheaded on top of this hill.

pois.name: St John's Church
pois.reason: Baroque university church on the Great Courtyard
pois.hook: Vilnius University's church, dating from 1387, with a Vilnian Baroque belfry.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Johns in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Vilnius University Great Courtyard 1, Vilnius, Lithuania - Diliff.jpg
pois.description: The Church of St. Johns, officially named St. John the Baptist and St. John the Apostle and Evangelist, is located at the Old Town of Vilnius, Lithuania and dominates the university ensemble. The church is dedicated to both John the Baptist and John the Evangelist.

pois.name: Vilnius University
pois.reason: Old university with a maze of Renaissance courtyards
pois.hook: Lithuania's first and largest university, a maze of Renaissance courtyards.
pois.description: Vilnius University is a public research university, which is the first and largest university in Lithuania, as well as one of the oldest and most prominent higher education institutions in Central and Eastern Europe. Today, it is Lithuania's leading research institution.

pois.name: Adam Mickiewicz Monument
pois.reason: Poet's monument in the square behind St Anne's
pois.hook: Gediminas Jokūbonis's granite poet from 1984, between St Anne's and the Neris.
pois.description: Adam Mickiewicz Monument in Vilnius, Lithuania is a monument in the vicinity of the Saint Anne's Church and the Bernardine Monastery, by Maironio Street along the shores of the Neris River.

pois.name: Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights
pois.reason: Former KGB headquarters with prison cells in the basement
pois.hook: Soviet NKVD and KGB prison from 1940 to 1991, with cells in the basement.
pois.commonsCategory: Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights
pois.description: The Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights in Vilnius is dedicated to showing artifacts and records from the 50-year Soviet occupation of Lithuania.

pois.name: Vilnius Picture Gallery
pois.reason: Lithuanian painting from the 16th to the 19th century in the Chodkiewicz Palace
pois.hook: Lithuanian painting from the 16th to the 19th century in the Chodkiewicz Palace.

pois.name: Bernardine Church
pois.reason: Gothic Franciscan church next to St Anne's
pois.hook: Gothic church of Francis of Assisi and Bernardino of Siena, next to St Anne's.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Francis of Assisi in Vilnius
pois.description: The Church of St. Francis and St. Bernardino is a Roman Catholic church in the Old Town of Vilnius, Lithuania. It is located next to St. Anne's Church.

pois.name: Theatre, Music and Cinema Museum
pois.hook: Lithuanian theatre, music and film history inside the Minor Radvila Palace.
pois.localName: Lietuvos teatro, muzikos ir kino muziejus
pois.commonsCategory: Lithuanian Theatre, Music and Film Museum

pois.name: Adam Mickiewicz Memorial Apartment
pois.hook: The poet's own flat, where Mickiewicz worked on his poem Grażyna.

pois.name: Presidential Palace of the Republic of Lithuania
pois.reason: Seat of Lithuania's President on Daukanto Square
pois.hook: The president's seat began in the 14th century as the Bishop of Vilnius's home.
pois.description: The Presidential Palace is the official residence and workplace of the president of Lithuania. Located in Vilnius Old Town, Lithuania.

pois.name: Grand Duke Gediminas
pois.reason: Statue of the city's legendary founder on Cathedral Square
pois.hook: The ruler who made Vilnius his capital in 1323, cast in 1996.
pois.commonsImage: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania and Gediminas Monument, Vilnius.jpg

pois.name: Užupis Angel
pois.reason: Bronze angel on a column in the middle of Užupis
pois.hook: Romas Vilčiauskas's bronze angel, raised on its column in 2002.

pois.name: Church of St Peter and St Paul
pois.reason: Plain outside; inside over 2000 white stucco figures
pois.hook: Plain outside; inside, some 2,000 white stucco figures by Giovanni Pietro Perti.
pois.localName: Šv. apaštalų Petro ir Povilo bažnyčia
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Peter and St. Paul in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Vilnius Sts Peter et Paul Church 01.jpg
pois.description: The Church of St. Peter and St. Paul is a Roman Catholic church located in the Antakalnis neighbourhood of Vilnius, Lithuania, designed and built by Jan Zaor of Kraków. It is the centerpiece of a former monastery complex of the Canons Regular of the Lateran.

pois.name: Literatų Street
pois.reason: Wall of small artworks for writers linked to Vilnius
pois.hook: Some 200 plaques to writers tied to Vilnius, added since 2009.
pois.description: Literatų Street is one of streets in the Old Town of Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania.

pois.name: Church of the Holy Spirit
pois.reason: Late-baroque Dominican church with a richly decorated interior
pois.hook: High and late Baroque church whose cupola stands out over the Old Town.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of the Holy Spirit in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Dominikonų Street in Vilnius, Lithuania in 2007.jpg
pois.description: Dominican Church of the Holy Spirit, Vilnius is a church in Vilnius, Lithuania, a monument of high and late Baroque. Crowned with a cupola, it stands out in the panorama of the old town and can be seen from surrounding streets.

pois.name: Abramowicz Palace
pois.hook: Palace on Town Hall Square, now owned by the Juozas Tallat-Kelpša conservatory.
pois.description: Abramavičiai Palace is a building in Vilnius Old Town, Rotušė square. Currently it is owned by Vilnius Juozas Tallat-Kelpša conservatory.

pois.name: St Paraskeva Orthodox Church
pois.reason: Historic church, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: The oldest Eastern Orthodox church in Lithuania.
pois.commonsCategory: St. Parasceve Orthodox Church in Vilnius
pois.description: St. Paraskeva Church is the oldest Eastern Orthodox church in Lithuania, located in the capital Vilnius, belonging to the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.

pois.name: Church of St Theresa
pois.reason: Historic church, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: Completed in 1650, the oldest towerless Baroque monument in Lithuania.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Theresa in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of Saint Teresa and Gate of Dawn in Vilnius, Lithuania (June 14, 2015).jpg
pois.description: Church of St. Theresa is a Roman Catholic church in Vilnius' Old Town, close to the Gate of Dawn. It was completed in 1650, and it is dedicated to Teresa of Ávila.

pois.name: St Michael's Church
pois.reason: Renaissance church; now the Church Heritage Museum
pois.hook: Former Renaissance church by the Vilnia, now the Church Heritage Museum.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Michael in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of St. Michael in Vilnius02(js).jpg
pois.description: St Michael's Church or St. Michael the Archangel Church is a former Roman Catholic church in Vilnius' Old Town, on the right bank of the Vilnia River. It now hosts the Church Heritage Museum.

pois.name: Basilian Church of the Holy Trinity
pois.reason: Place of worship, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: Built by Konstanty Ostrogski in thanks for victory at the Battle of Orsha.
pois.localName: Švč. Trejybės Graikų apeigų katalikų bažnyčia
pois.commonsCategory: Monastery of the Holy Trinity, Vilnius
pois.description: Monastery of the Holy Trinity is a monastery built in Vilnius by the Ruthenian Church and Grand Hetman of Lithuania Konstanty Ostrogski as a thanksgiving to the God for the victory in Battle of Orsha. It now belongs to the Order of Saint Basil the Great and the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church.

pois.name: Church of St Catherine
pois.reason: Historic church, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: Baroque church founded in 1618 by Hetman Jan Karol Chodkiewicz.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Catherine in Vilnius
pois.description: The Church of St. Catherine is a Roman Catholic church in Vilnius' Old Town. It was founded by the Hetman of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Voivode of Vilnius Jan Karol Chodkiewicz in 1618.

pois.name: Cathedral Bell Tower
pois.reason: Free-standing bell tower of the Cathedral
pois.hook: A 13th-century defensive tower that became the cathedral belfry in the 1500s.

pois.name: St Casimir's Church
pois.reason: Historic church, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: Built in 1618, the first and oldest Baroque church in Vilnius.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Casimir in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of St. Casimir in Vilnius (Wilno).JPG
pois.description: The Church of St. Casimir is a Roman Catholic church in Vilnius' Old Town, close to the Vilnius' Town Hall. It is the first and the oldest baroque church in Vilnius, built in 1618.

pois.name: Yugen Tea
pois.hook: Japanese tea bar and studio in Užupis, with tastings and teaware.
pois.description: Teahouse café with outdoor seating, an all-vegetarian menu and vegan options. Open Tue–Sat 12:00–20:00, Sun 12:00–19:00.

pois.name: Bastion of the City Wall
pois.hook: Bastion of the old city defences, tied to the legend of the Basilisk.

pois.name: Cathedral of the Theotokos
pois.reason: Cathedral, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: Episcopal see of the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.
pois.localName: Vilniaus Dievo Motinos Ėmimo į Dangų katedra
pois.commonsCategory: Orthodox Cathedral of the Dormition of the Theotokos in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Cathedral of the Theotokos by Augustas Didzgalvis.jpg
pois.description: The Cathedral of the Theotokos in Vilnius is the episcopal see of the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.

pois.name: Lokys
pois.hook: Historic Lithuanian cooking built on game and forest produce.

pois.name: St Nicholas Orthodox Church
pois.reason: Historic church, well-known landmark, popular photo spot
pois.hook: One of Vilnius's oldest Orthodox churches, dating from 1514.
pois.localName: Vilniaus Šv. Mikolajaus Stebukladario palaikų Pernešimo cerkvė
pois.commonsCategory: St. Nicholas Orthodox Church in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: St. Nicholas Orthodox Church, Vilnius, Lithuania - Diliff.jpg
pois.description: Church of the Transfer of the Relics of St. Nicholas the Wonderworker in Vilnius or St. Nicholas Church is one of the oldest Eastern Orthodox churches in Vilnius, Lithuania, and belongs to the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.

pois.name: Divine Mercy Sanctuary
pois.reason: Place of worship, popular photo spot
pois.hook: Shrine to the Divine Mercy, the devotion begun by Faustina Kowalska.
pois.description: The Divine Mercy Sanctuary of Vilnius or the Holy Trinity Church is a shrine in Vilnius dedicated to the Divine Mercy, a devotion originated by Faustina Kowalska.

pois.name: Green Bridge
pois.hook: Built in 1952; its 16th-century forerunner was the city's oldest bridge.
pois.description: The Green Bridge is a bridge over the Neris River in Vilnius, Lithuania, that connects the city center with the district of Šnipiškės. The original 16th-century bridge was the oldest bridge in Vilnius.

pois.name: King Mindaugas Bridge
pois.hook: Opened in 2003 for the 750th anniversary of King Mindaugas's coronation.
pois.description: The Mindaugas Bridge is a bridge in Vilnius, Lithuania. It crosses Neris River and connects Žirmūnai elderate with the Old Town of Vilnius.

pois.name: St Ignatius Church
pois.hook: Serves as the cathedral of Lithuania's Military Ordinariate.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Ignatius in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of St Ignatius in Vilnius2.jpg
pois.description: The Cathedral of St. Ignatius of Loyola also called Church of St. Ignatius is a religious building of the Roman Catholic Church that serves as the cathedral of the Military Ordinariate of Lithuania. It is located in the capital, Vilnius.

pois.name: All Saints Church
pois.hook: Baroque church built in 1620–1631 and adapted for the Carmelites.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of All Saints in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of All Saints in Vilnius, Lithuania in 2007.jpg
pois.description: The Church of All Saints is a Baroque-style church in Vilnius, Lithuania. The church was built between 1620–1631 and was adopted for Carmelites' needs.

pois.name: Choral Synagogue
pois.hook: Orthodox Jewish congregation, officially named Taharat Ha-Kodesh.
pois.description: The Choral Synagogue of Vilnius, officially, Taharat Ha-Kodesh Choral Synagogue in Vilnius, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 39 Pylimo Street, in the Old Town of Vilnius, in the Vilnius County of Lithuania.

pois.name: Lithuanian National Philharmonic
pois.hook: Lithuania's oldest and largest state concert body: classical, jazz, new music.
pois.description: Lithuanian National Philharmonic Society also known by its abbreviation LNPS, is a national cultural institution and the largest and oldest state-owned concert organisation in Lithuania headquartered in the nations capital of Vilnius.

pois.name: Radziwiłł Palace
pois.hook: Late Renaissance palace built in 1646–1653 for Hetman Janusz Radziwiłł.
pois.description: Radvilas Palace is a Late Renaissance palace in the Old Town of Vilnius, Lithuania.

pois.name: MO Museum
pois.hook: 6,000 modern and contemporary works gathered by two scientist-philanthropists.
pois.description: The MO Museum is a modern art museum in Vilnius, Lithuania. As a private initiative of Lithuanian scientists and philanthropists Danguolė Butkienė and Viktoras Butkus, it functioned as an art museum without walls for about ten years.

pois.name: Orthodox Church of the Holy Spirit
pois.hook: Rebuilt in Vilnian Baroque in 1749–1753; seat of the Orthodox diocese.
pois.commonsCategory: Orthodox Church of the Holy Spirit in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Orthodox Church of the Holy Spirit in Vilnius2.JPG
pois.description: The Orthodox Church of the Holy Spirit is a Russian Orthodox church in the Vilnius Old Town, capital of Lithuania, rebuilt 1749–1753 in the Vilnian Baroque style. The monastery serves as the headquarters of the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.

pois.name: Crooked Hill
pois.hook: Hillfort site, one of four that formed a complex on both banks of the Vilnia.

pois.name: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre
pois.hook: Lithuania's only university-level arts school: music, theatre, dance and film.
pois.commonsCategory: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre
pois.description: The Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre in Vilnius, Lithuania, is a state-supported conservatory that trains students in music, theatre, and multimedia arts.

pois.name: Energy and Technology Museum
pois.hook: Lithuania's largest technology museum, inside a former Vilnius power plant.
pois.description: Energy and Technology Museum is an institution dedicated to researching and presenting energy history, the industrial heritage of Lithuania, and the history of Vilnius. It is housed in a former Vilnius power plant.

pois.name: Raduszkiewicz Palace
pois.hook: Now the headquarters of the Lithuanian Union of Architects.
pois.description: The Raduškevičius Palace is a building in Vilnius, Kalvarijų st. 1. Currently it is headquarters of the Lithuanian Union of Architects.

pois.name: Orthodox Church of St Constantine and St Michael
pois.hook: Russian Orthodox church known locally as the Romanov church.
pois.localName: Vilniaus Šv. Konstantino ir Michailo cerkvė
pois.commonsCategory: Orthodox Church of St. Michael and St. Constantine in Vilnius
pois.description: The Orthodox Church of St. Michael and St. Constantine is a Russian Orthodox church in Vilnius, Lithuania, belonging to the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.

pois.name: Vileišis Palace
pois.hook: Neo-baroque ensemble built in 1904–1906 for publisher Petras Vileišis.
pois.description: Vileišis Palace is a Neo-baroque style architectural ensemble in Vilnius, Lithuania, built for Petras Vileišis. Vileišis was a prominent Lithuanian engineer, political activist, publisher, and philanthropist who commissioned the palace in 1904 and supervised its construction.

pois.name: Church of Our Lady of Consolation
pois.hook: Built by the Augustinians in 1746–1768, the last Vilnian Baroque landmark.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Consolation in Vilnius
pois.description: Church of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Consolation is a Roman Catholic church in the Vilnius Old Town which was built by the Augustinians in 1746–1768. It is the last landmark of the Vilnian Baroque architectural style.

pois.name: Church of the Ascension
pois.hook: Begun in 1695 and finished only 35 years later for lack of funds.
pois.description: Church of the Ascension is a Roman Catholic church in the Vilnius Old Town. Its construction began in 1695, but due to the lack of funding it was completed only after 35 years in 1730 and in the same year was it was consecrated as Church of the Ascension.

pois.name: St Nicholas Church
pois.hook: The oldest surviving church in Lithuania, dating from 1387.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Nicholas in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Front façade of the Church of Saint Nicholas in Vilnius, Lithuania.jpg
pois.description: Saint Nicholas Church is the oldest surviving church in Lithuania, built in the Old Town of the capital city Vilnius.

pois.name: Contemporary Art Centre
pois.hook: George Maciunas's Fluxus cabinet has been on permanent show here since 1997.
pois.description: Contemporary Art Centre – art institution, established in 1992 by Lithuanian Ministry of Culture. CAC has replaced the Arts Exhibition Palace and took over its building in Vilnius, 2 Vokiečių street.

pois.name: Pachamama Dinner Club
pois.hook: Peruvian fusion cooking, burgers included.

pois.name: Skersvėjis
pois.hook: Revived Užupis lane named after Jonas Mekas, lined with galleries and boutiques.

pois.name: RoseHip Vegan Bistro - Pylimo
pois.hook: Everything on the menu is vegan.

pois.name: St Nicholas Orthodox Church at Lukiškės Prison
pois.hook: Orthodox church that served Lukiškės Prison.
pois.commonsCategory: St. Nicholas Orthodox Church in Lukiškės prison

pois.name: Vyninė Saint Germain
pois.hook: Wine bar serving modern French cooking from a seasonal menu.

pois.name: Alaus biblioteka
pois.hook: Shelves hold hundreds of beers instead of books, with 17 more on tap.

pois.name: Namai be gliuteno.Vilnius
pois.hook: Gluten-free bakes of its own making: biscuits, cakes and bread.

pois.name: Church of Our Lady of the Sign
pois.hook: Orthodox church raised in 1903 in the Žvėrynas district.
pois.localName: Vilniaus Dievo Motinos ikonos „Ženklas iš dangaus“ cerkvė
pois.commonsCategory: Orthodox Church of Revelation of the Holy Mother of God in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Orthodox Church of Revelation of the Holy Mother of God Domes, Vilnius, Lithuania - Diliff.jpg
pois.description: Our Lady of the Sign Church is an Eastern Orthodox church in the Žvėrynas district of Vilnius, built in 1903, belonging to the Russian Orthodox Diocese of Lithuania.

pois.name: Church of the Holy Cross
pois.hook: Began as a chapel in 1543; towers added in 1725, interior after a 1737 fire.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of the Holy Cross in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of the Holy Cross in Vilnius Bonifratri3.jpg
pois.description: Church of the Holy Cross is a Roman Catholic church in the Vilnius Old Town. Initially, in 1543 a chapel was built which was later expanded and rebuilt.

pois.name: Motif
pois.hook: Japanese fusion cooking with European touches.

pois.name: Užantis - sendaikčių parduotuvėlė
pois.hook: Tiny Užupis shop of vintage homeware, records and photography.

pois.name: Church of St Bartholomew
pois.hook: Built in 1824, the only church in Vilnius with Mass in Belarusian.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Bartholomew in Vilnius
pois.description: Church of St. Bartholomew is a Roman Catholic church in Užupis, Vilnius which was built in 1824. It is the only church in Vilnius where the masses are held in the Belarusian language.

pois.name: Fionos cukrainė
pois.hook: Handmade mousse and classic cakes, plus macarons.

pois.name: Old Theatre of Vilnius
pois.hook: Opened in 1913; Lithuania's only professional theatre playing in Russian.
pois.description: Old Theatre of Vilnius, built in 1913 as Pohulanka Theatre and formerly known as Russian Drama Theatre of Lithuania and other names, is a theatre in the Old Town of Vilnius. It is the only professional theatre in Lithuania that stages performances in Russian.

pois.name: AJ Šokoladas
pois.hook: Café of a chocolate maker that has been at it for two decades.

pois.name: Embankment Arch
pois.hook: Also known as Vamzdis, the pipe; an arch set on the embankment in 2009.

pois.name: Lutheran Church
pois.hook: The only Evangelical Lutheran church in Vilnius, with a parish of 600.
pois.description: Evangelical Lutheran Church is a Lutheran church in the Vilnius Old Town. Its parish has 600 members and it is the only Evangelical Lutheran church in Vilnius.

pois.name: Brussels Mussels
pois.hook: Belgian-style pub where mussel dishes and Belgian waffles are favourites.

pois.name: Easter Egg Sculpture
pois.hook: A margutis, the decorated Easter egg, sculpted in 2003.

pois.name: Lukiškės Square
pois.hook: Vilnius's largest square, some 4 hectares, ringed by ministries and courts.
pois.description: Lukiškės Square is the largest square (about 4 hectares in Vilnius, Lithuania, located in the center of the city. A major street in Vilnius, Gediminas Avenue, passes by the southern border of the square.

pois.name: 14Horses
pois.hook: Contemporary Baltic–Scandinavian cooking within the walls of Vainai Palace.

pois.name: Church of St Philip and St James
pois.hook: Known for its painting of the Mother of God of Lukiškės.
pois.localName: Šv. apaštalų Pilypo ir Jokūbo bažnyčia
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Philip and St. Jacob in Vilnius
pois.description: Church of Saints Philip and James is a Roman Catholic church in Vilnius' Old Town, near the Lukiškės Square. It is famous for the Mother of God of Lukiškės painting.

pois.name: Lithuanian National Drama Theatre
pois.hook: Founded in 1940; its façade carries Stanislovas Kuzma's Feast of the Muses.
pois.description: Lithuanian National Drama Theatre, located on Gediminas Avenue in Vilnius, is one of Lithuania's most prominent publicly funded performing arts venues and cultural institutions. Founded as a Vilnius State Theatre in 1940, it became Lithuanian National Drama Theatre in 1998.

pois.name: Būsi trečias
pois.hook: Beer brewed in the cellar beneath the tables, with six taps and board games.

pois.name: Crooked Nose & Coffee Stories
pois.hook: Coffee roaster that also runs tastings and subscriptions.

pois.name: Church of the Immaculate Conception
pois.hook: Finished in 1925 without its towers, halted by the Depression and the war.
pois.localName: Švč. Mergelės Marijos Nekaltojo Prasidėjimo bažnyčia
pois.commonsCategory: Church of the Immaculate Conception in Vilnius
pois.description: Church of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a Roman Catholic church in Žvėrynas, one of the neighborhoods of Vilnius, which was for the most part completed in 1925.

pois.name: First Swallows
pois.hook: Juozas Mikėnas's bronze, first made as a monument to Soviet cosmonauts.

pois.name: Biblioteka Outside
pois.hook: Hundreds of beers shelved like library books, plus tastings.

pois.name: Church of St Raphael the Archangel
pois.hook: Dating from 1709, next to a former Jesuit monastery.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. Raphael in Vilnius
pois.commonsImage: Church of the St Raphael the Archangel in Vilnius12.jpg
pois.description: Church of St. Raphael the Archangel is a Roman Catholic church in Šnipiškės, Vilnius. Former Jesuits monastery ensemble is located nearby which currently is used by the Department of Cultural Heritage of Lithuania.

pois.name: Šnekutis
pois.hook: Cepelinai, cold beetroot soup and craft beer, to reggae and alternative music.

pois.name: AJ Šokoladas
pois.hook: Restaurant of a chocolate manufactory with twenty years of history.

pois.name: Church of the Sacred Heart
pois.hook: Built in 1694–1756 and now enclosed within a prison, closed to worship.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in Vilnius
pois.description: Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus is a Roman Catholic church in the Vilnius Old Town, which was built in 1694–1756 and consecrated in 1756.

pois.name: Vilnius City Museum
pois.hook: Opened in spring 2021 with little-known stories of the city.

pois.name: Galo de Porto
pois.hook: Portuguese cooking in the Old Town, with signature steaks on the menu.

pois.name: Soviki
pois.hook: The name is short for Sous Vide Kitchen; there is a second branch in Trakai.

pois.name: Žirmūnai Bridge
pois.hook: Designed by a Leningrad institute in 1964 and built across the Neris in 1965.
pois.description: Žirmūnai Bridge is a bridge across Neris River, that connects Žirmūnai and Antakalnis districts of Vilnius. This is a pier ferroconcrete bridge 181 meters (594 ft) long.

pois.name: Brussels Mussels

pois.name: Italala Caffè

pois.name: Kanapinė krautuvė
pois.hook: Organic hemp products, sold from a café.

pois.name: Karaite Kenesa
pois.hook: Prayer house of the Karaite Jewish congregation, in the Žvėrynas district.
pois.description: The Vilnius Kenesa is a Qaraite Jewish congregation and synagogue, or kenesa, located at 6 Liubarto Street, in Žvėrynas, one of the neighborhoods of Vilnius, in the Vilnius County of Lithuania.

pois.name: Bernardine Garden
pois.hook: Park on the Vilnia that hosts an amateur Ostap Bender chess championship.
pois.description: The Bernardine Garden, previously known as Sereikiškės Park, is a public park in the city of Vilnius, Lithuania. It is located on the left bank of the Vilnia River between the Gediminas Tower and Bernardine Monastery and covers over 9 hectares.

pois.name: Elska Coffee
pois.hook: Freshly roasted coffee beans and matcha, plus brewing gear.

pois.name: Reformed Church
pois.hook: Karol Podczaszyński's design, built 1830–35, with a new organ added in 2008.
pois.description: Evangelical Reformed Church is a Continental Reformed Protestantic church in the Vilnius Old Town which was built in 1830–1835 according to a project of Karol Podczaszyński. In 2008 a new organ was installed in the church.

pois.name: Coffee Spells
pois.hook: Vilnius-roasted speciality coffee scoring 84+ SCA points, plus tastings.

pois.name: Forum Palace
pois.hook: Shopping centre and indoor arena that often hosts concerts.
pois.description: Forum Palace is a commercial center and indoor arena in Vilnius. The arena is located near to the Vilnius financial centre in Konstitucija avenue.

pois.name: Iron Wolf Bridge
pois.hook: Named after the Iron Wolf legend, linking Naujamiestis with Žvėrynas.
pois.description: The Iron Wolf Bridge is a bridge over the Neris River in Vilnius, Lithuania. Named after the legend of Iron Wolf, the bridge connects Naujamiestis with the districts of Žvėrynas and Šnipiškės, as the roundabout is situated at the administrative line.

pois.name: Arena Vilnius
pois.hook: Vilnius's largest arena, opened in 2004 for basketball games and concerts.
pois.description: Arena Vilnius, located in the southern part of Verkiai elderate of Vilnius, is the largest arena in Vilnius and second largest in Lithuania. It generally hosts basketball games as well as concerts.

pois.name: Candy POP
pois.hook: Sweets, snacks and drinks imported from the US, Asia and beyond.

pois.name: St George's Church
pois.hook: Built by the Radziwiłł family as their mausoleum; consecrated in 1765.
pois.commonsCategory: Church of St. George in Vilnius
pois.description: Church of St. George is a Roman Catholic church in the Vilnius Old Town which was completed and consecrated in 1765. The church and nearby monastery complex was built by the Radziwiłł family and served as family's mausoleum.

pois.name: Strange Love
pois.hook: Roasting coffee locally since 2015.

pois.name: Brew

pois.name: Keistoteka

pois.name: Saint Malo Restaurant

pois.name: Słuszko Palace
pois.hook: Baroque palace on the Neris bank, in what was once the Antakalnis suburb.
pois.description: Slushko Palace in Vilnius, Lithuania is a Baroque palace situated on the left bank of Neris River in the Old Town elderate, former Antakalnis suburb of the city.

pois.name: Urban Garden

pois.commonsCategory: House-museum of Venclova Family in Vilnius

pois.name: Empty Brain Resort
pois.hook: Venue for DIY music and art events.

pois.name: Tuskulėnai Manor Palace
pois.hook: Excavations in 1994–1996 found 706 bodies here; only 40 were identified.
pois.description: Tuskulėnai Manor is a neoclassical manor in Žirmūnai elderate of Vilnius, Lithuania. It is perhaps best known as a burial ground for people executed by the KGB in 1944–1947.

pois.name: Akropolis
pois.reason: Big mall by the Neris with an indoor ice rink
pois.hook: Largest shopping mall in the Baltics by floor area, with an indoor ice rink.
pois.description: Akropolis is the largest shopping mall in the Baltics by floor area, a shopping center and entertainment center in Vilnius, the Lithuanian capital. It was built in Šeškinė by Akropolis Group in 2002 and opened in April 2002.
